sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: One figure, read off the single returned row: the store dimension holds 74 version records. Each is one row describing one shop's premises over one trading period, so this counts RECORDS and not shops a customer could walk into today — the web shop's single row is in it, and so are all 16 rows for premises that have since closed. What it does NOT count: sites (67 distinct location_code sit behind these 74 rows, 6 places having been re-let), and trading shops (57, which is what "how many stores do we have" asks). No time window applies, because this is the dimension as it currently stands rather than a history of it.

Both defaults that normally bite on a Store subject are deliberately withheld: the `physical` default (store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel) and the `active` default (store.resolution.active_is_the_absent_close_date), because store.resolution.a_version_is_a_row_and_a_row_has_no_channel names this question verbatim and rules that a question about the RECORD takes neither. SELECT
  store_key,
  location_code,
  store_name,
  country_code,
  state,
  open_date,
  close_date,
  status_annotation,
  square_metres
FROM contoso_served.dim_store
value.means: Every version record the store dimension holds — 74 rows, one per premises per trading period, each row being one recorded version of a shop. The web shop's row (store_key 999999, location_code -1) is in, and so are all 16 rows of premises that have since closed. These are not 74 trading shops: they are 74 records, standing over 67 distinct sites, 6 of which carry more than one row because a place can be re-let.

readings.could_also_mean: the sites those rows stand on, which is 67 distinct location_code — but that is the Location concept, and dim_store.store_key is declared `finer_than: location_code`, so versions never roll down into places
readings.declaration: store.resolution.a_version_is_a_row_and_a_row_has_no_channel: "a question asks what the store dimension RECORDS ... cover every row of dim_store ... 74 rows over 67 distinct location_code"

readings.took: everything the dimension holds, including the 16 rows of premises that have closed and the 1 online sentinel row
readings.could_also_mean: only the currently-trading premises, which would be 57 (74 less the 16 closed less the online row) — a materially different figure
